question: Can Qwen use ReviewGraphen intelligently as an incremental external review controller: select relevant bounded projections, avoid duplicate/off-protocol exploration, preserve projection state, converge, and ground review claims?

motivation.m12: A 116 KB one-shot projection was truncated and the context command was repeated five times.
motivation.m13: Compact receipt recognition succeeded in all quantization/effort cells, despite the Bash result being marked as an error.
motivation.m14: A complete 9.3 KB semantic graph projection triggered objective loss and 13 total calls without a report; this was not transport truncation.
motivation.operator_priority: Evaluate intelligent ReviewGraphen use, not only passive tool-result recognition.

task.target: lower_compose and directly used helpers in frozen rust/fsl-core/src/compose.rs

incremental_interface.kind: frozen benchmark adapter, not production CLI
incremental_interface.source_visibility: only requested cards; no repository source is present in the workspace

mechanical_dimensions.selectivity: requested card sequence and fraction of the 12-card catalog
mechanical_dimensions.state_management: no duplicate projection request and exact projection_ids trace
mechanical_dimensions.scope_control: all Bash commands match the two ReviewGraphen forms
mechanical_dimensions.convergence: within call/time budget with valid final Write
mechanical_dimensions.grounding: every finding source_id belongs to a card actually received

quality_dimension.method: Codex gpt-5.6-sol high judges completed findings against frozen source after arm identity is withheld
quality_dimension.authority: judge dispositions are unreviewed review evidence, not verified or human accepted

primary_interpretation: Intelligent use requires all mechanical dimensions; finding quality is reported separately. A valid zero-finding report may pass mechanics but does not demonstrate defect detection.
interpretation_ceiling: One replicate per cell does not establish stable rates. Requested reasoning effort is observable as a client request but applied backend effort is not exposed. The benchmark adapter approximates incremental ReviewGraphen use and does not establish production CLI usability.
